items.title: [PD] Deferred decode-side KV release for aborts mid-transfer
items.body:
## Motivation

Aborting a decode request (long-ITL abort/timeout, `/abort_request`) while its prefill→decode KV transfer is still in flight frees the request's KV pages and req-pool slot **immediately**, but does **not** cancel the transfer. The next request can then be allocated those same pages and have them overwritten by the earlier, still-in-flight write — the next request silently holds the first request's KV, with no error raised anywhere. This is the race [@ShangmingCai anticipated in #27372](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27372) ("we could introduce deferred release of decode-side KVCache to fix this"), the open bug in #32564, and the reason the `ABORT_ACK` handler in `mooncake/conn.py` carries a `TODO(shangming)` for exactly this mechanism.

It is also why an O(1) tail-pop free-slot change like #34876 is unsafe on the decode side today: LIFO reuse maximally shrinks the free→reuse window and maximizes the probability of hitting this race. This PR is the prerequisite that makes immediate slot reuse safe.

## What this does

An **env-gated deferred-release path**. When off (default) there is **zero behavior/perf change** — every new branch is behind an `enable_deferred_*` guard, and the wire format / free path are byte-identical. When on, an aborted request's KV pages, req-slot and metadata buffer are **held** until the prefill proves its transfer drained, then released.

**Prefill (`mooncake/conn.py`).** On an `ABORT` for an active room, mark the room `Failed` **first** (stops `add_transfer_request` from enqueuing new chunks), then register the ack target, and do **not** ack from the bootstrap thread. The single transfer worker that owns the room sends the `ABORT_ACK` — carrying its prefill rank — once the room's in-flight chunk has drained (at both the skip and completion sites, via `_maybe_ack_drained_abort`). Rooms already done/unknown ack immediately.

**Decode (`decode.py` + `common/conn.py`).** On the `Failed` poll (for a decode-initiated abort), instead of releasing, move the request to a held list with a deadline. `resolve_deferred_releases()` (called early every scheduler step) releases a room once **every prefill rank the abort was sent to** has acked (`is_abort_release_safe`) or the timeout fires. The per-room ack tracker is armed in `abort_request` when the `ABORT` is sent, so acks that arrive during the next forward step are captured.

### Why it's correct

- **Single-writer per room.** A room's chunks shard to one transfer queue served by exactly one worker thread (`session_port_sum % len(transfer_queues)`, one thread per queue), so a room's writes and its `_staging_outstanding` counter are single-writer. The ack is driven **entirely from that worker**, never the bootstrap thread, so it can't race an in-flight write. No new locks.
- **Dummy-proof denominator.** The decode requires an ack from **each** prefill rank it notified (`len(bootstrap_infos)`), not `required_prefill_response_num`. Every notified rank acks exactly once — real ranks after their write drains, dummy/already-done ranks immediately — so reaching the count provably means no prefill can still be writing to those pages. Over/under-counting from dummy ranks (which would cause early release = corruption) is impossible.
- **Timeout backstop.** If an ack never arrives (dead prefill rank, stuck send), the pages are force-released after the timeout — matching the ~30s mooncake transfer ceiling noted in #27372.

### Coverage / fallback (honest scope)

The fast (ack-driven) release fires for the primary corruption scenario — an abort while the transfer is actively in flight on the notified ranks. Cases where a rank already concluded before the abort fall back to the timeout hold (safe, never an early release). This is a deliberately lighter alternative to the full lease/barrier rework in #32564; it reuses the existing `ABORT`/`ABORT_ACK` channel and changes only *when* the ack is sent and *when* decode releases.

## Env

- `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_DEFERRED_DECODE_KV_RELEASE` (bool, default `False`)
- `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_DEFERRED_DECODE_KV_RELEASE_TIMEOUT` (float seconds, default `30.0`)

## Tests

`test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_deferred_decode_kv_release.py`:
- ack aggregation: release-safe only after all required ranks ack; duplicate-rank ack does not over-count; single-rank fast path; state cleared.
- `resolve_deferred_releases`: holds until drained then releases exactly once (frees metadata idx, resets `bootstrap_room`, clears deferred state, nulls receiver); releases on timeout without ack; no-op when nothing deferred.

## Validation status

⚠️ **Draft — pending PD-cluster integration validation.** The unit-tested decode-side state machine and the correctness argument above are done, but I have not yet run this on a live prefill/decode Mooncake deployment (e.g. the 2P1D H200 setup #32564 used, with in-flight-donor-abort victim-reuse probes). Marking draft until that passes.

## Checklist

- [x] Format with pre-commit (black/isort)
- [x] Add unit tests
- [ ] Provide accuracy/speed benchmark results (N/A — abort-path correctness change; no kernel/throughput impact when off)
- [x] Code style

Related: #27372, #32564, #34876

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---

## Self-review hardening (2nd commit)

An adversarial multi-agent review of the first commit surfaced and fixed several real issues:

- **Corruption (prefill ordering):** mark the room `Failed` **before** registering the ack target — the reverse order let the worker drain + ACK while the room wasn't yet `Failed`, so a newly-enqueued chunk could still write to already-freed decode pages.
- **Corruption (room-reuse pollution):** `bootstrap_room` is not globally unique; a stale/late ACK could satisfy a later request reusing the room and release it early. The ack tracker is now armed/reset per abort episode (in `abort_request` when the ABORT is sent) and drops acks for unregistered rooms.
- **Functionality (ack timing):** arming the tracker at defer-time lost almost every ACK (a full forward step runs between `abort()` and deferral), degrading every fast release to a timeout. Now armed when the ABORT is sent.
- **Leak/functional (resolve reachability):** `resolve_deferred_releases` now runs early and unconditionally (was behind the retraction early-return and the polling gate; and independent of `release_rids` in the PP path), so held slots still time out under memory pressure.
- **Corruption/cascade (resolve):** commit the surviving set before releasing and isolate a failing `_do_release`, so one error can't double-free a metadata idx or brick the decode loop.
- Only decode-initiated aborts are deferred (`abort_notified`); prefill-initiated failures release immediately.

Added regression tests for reuse-pollution, ack-before-register drop, and release-exception isolation.

items.title: [AMD] Use HIP batched copies for HiCache write-back
items.body:
## Motivation

ROCm staged HiCache write-back currently submits one `hipMemcpyAsync` per page even though HIP 7.1+ provides `hipMemcpyBatchAsync`. This reduces CPU-side submission overhead for page-first D2H write-back while preserving the existing fallback on older runtimes or unsupported calls.

## Modifications

- Dynamically resolve `hipMemcpyBatchAsync` on ROCm 7.1+.
- Submit large page copies as one batch with null attributes, as required by the HIP API.
- Retain per-page fallback for old runtimes, missing symbols, and unsupported calls.
- Add a ROCm large-page correctness case that exceeds the existing 128 KiB batch threshold.

## Accuracy Tests

MI355X, ROCm 7.2.26015:

- `pytest -q -s test/registered/kernels/ops/kvcache/test_hicache_page_first_write_back.py`: 13 passed.
- `rocprofv3` confirms the large-page case issues `hipMemcpyBatchAsync`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Base-A / Candidate / Base-B on one idle MI355X, 16 MHA/MLA shapes, 8/32 layers, 1/4/16/64 pages, page size 256, 40 repetitions per shape:

- Host submission latency: 3.27% lower geomean; all 16 shapes improved.
- End-to-end synchronized D2H latency: +0.01% geomean (neutral, as expected because transferred bytes are unchanged).
- Largest individual submission reduction: 7.01%.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add and run unit tests.
- [x] Provide correctness and speed results.
- [ ] Run repository CI.

items.title: [Model] Add native SenseNova U1 multimodal generation and interleave serving
items.body: ## Summary This PR adds native SenseNova U1 support to main SGLang, including: - native language and multimodal-understanding execution; - native bounded flow matching for image generation; - OpenAI-compatible T2I and IT2I image APIs; - flow-prefill CUDA graph capture and replay; - scheduler-owned text-to-image-to-text interleave continuation; - deterministic, batch-size-invariant interleave image generation; - reusable official-HF versus native end-to-end benchmark tooling. The final cross-batch correctness fix is commit `581e47848d6791e5134c19ecd9763283fdd547b9`. It prevents the internal flow child from reusing parent KV generated under a concurrency-dependent text batch. The child remains scheduler-owned and request-isolated, but recomputes its flow conditioning with a Radix prefix match limit of zero. Parent decode state, parking, image attachment, re-encoding, and resumed decode remain unchanged. Hermes first-review hardening is commit `48b91296805e66f45c3a75ac4eaba6d40ed4a62a`. It adds bounded parsed-upload reads, request propagation, active-RID aborts, and strict numeric validation. The remaining receive-boundary hardening is commit `dafbc308ea8fb998ad2828a15beda31b783fe7d8`. It enforces the total edit multipart cap before Starlette materializes `UploadFile`, validates declared and observed body lengths, and fails closed on interrupted or malformed streams. This commit is pushed to `waltstephen/sensenova-u1-native-main`, which updates existing `sgl-project/sglang#35038`; no new PR was created. The warmed-performance completion is commit `7b23547014ec6387f7efdd27972729196fb2063d`. It adds bounded exact-text and flow caches, fixes decode-graph MRoPE staging, preserves multi-image flow-prefix identity, and passes the approved H100 BS1/8/16, T2I, and fixed-work first-image targets without changing the workload, context, parity, determinism, or safety gates. ## Architecture The native interleave lifecycle is owned by main SGLang: 1. A bounded exact-text segment decodes until the model emits ``. 2. The scheduler parks the parent request state without finalizing it. The segment's private exact-text KV is released rather than inserted into shared Radix state. 3. A scheduler-owned prefix child recomputes the committed text/image prefix under a content-derived extra key, then a bounded internal flow request is created with: - a per-parent batch-isolation key; - an explicit image seed; - the same token/image geometry and MRoPE time index as the parent; - a Radix match limited to the canonical prefix child, never the concurrency-dependent parent segment. 4. Native flow matching runs inside SRT. No HF modeling fallback or serial HTTP wrapper is used. 5. The generated float16 image is converted to native vision features and attached to the parent request. 6. The next bounded exact-text segment recomputes or reuses its private prefix cache with the new image-context span and resumes the same parent request. The canonical flow-conditioning prefix is independently keyed by token IDs and multimodal feature bytes, bounded in scheduler state, and reset per image turn. Public T2I/IT2I requests retain their own prefix caching and the 64-token flow-prefill CUDA graph path. Implementation commit sequence: - `0db493a02`: native language core - `17a12f5ae`: native multimodal understanding - `fdf95b93a`: native flow execution - `f5a84ebb1`: native image APIs - `530b9f010`: flow-prefill CUDA graph - `7b1aa9826`: scheduler-owned interleave continuation - `899e9da56`: reusable interleave benchmark - `581e47848`: cross-batch invariant flow conditioning and benchmark regression - `48b912968`: image upload, cancellation, disconnect, and validation hardening - `dafbc308e`: pre-parser multipart request-boundary hardening and ASGI tests - `7b2354701`: warmed text/T2I/interleave optimization and fail-closed exact-text admission ### Image request lifecycle Image generation and edit requests now preserve the HTTP request lifecycle: 1. The FastAPI `Request` object is passed to every tokenizer-manager prefix and flow request. 2. Each active prefix/flow RID is tracked. 3. Client disconnects are detected by the tokenizer manager. 4. Task cancellation, disconnect exceptions, and other stage failures explicitly call `abort_request(rid)` before unwinding. 5. The async generator is closed after each stage. A pure ASGI middleware runs before multipart parsing. The total edit request cap is `2 * media_url_max_file_size_mb + 64 KiB`, covering image, optional mask, and multipart/form overhead. It requires one valid `Content-Length`, rejects a declared over-limit body before reading, counts actual receive-stream bytes, rejects understated/overstated lengths, and fails closed on disconnects. Compressed edit bodies are rejected because expansion would bypass the raw receive cap. The parsed `UploadFile` reader remains as defense in depth, consumes at most one byte beyond the per-file cap, and closes image and mask. Explicit user values are never replaced by truthiness defaults: - `n=0` is rejected rather than treated as `1`; - `num_inference_steps=0` is rejected rather than treated as `2`; - `flow_shift=0.0` is rejected rather than treated as `1.0`; - negative, nonfinite, and configured upper-bound violations are rejected. ## Correctness Benchmark contract: - model: `SenseNova-U1-8B-MoT-Interleaved-bd39` - prompt: `Say 'Here is the image:' then generate an image of a red apple. After the image, write at least 100 words describing it.` - seed: `20260813` - image: 256x256 - flow steps: 2 - generated text budget: 64 tokens - real turn: 6 text tokens, ``, flow, re-encode, 58 continued-text tokens - concurrency levels: 1, 2, 4, 8 - repetitions: 1 warmup plus 5 measured batches per level Results: - real text-to-image-to-text turn: PASS - shared output contract: PASS - generated text budget: 64/64 for HF and native - HF repeat determinism: PASS - native repeat determinism: PASS - native contract batch-size invariance: PASS - native image batch-size invariance: PASS - mapped logical request invariance across BS1/2/4/8: PASS - native image SHA-256 at every batch size: `dcc1e46748949c4da76065a98ab172562fe3fd954bb72f346dc18393ade93d33` - HF/native pre-image text tokens: exact - HF/native post-image wording: not token-exact after re-encoding, but both satisfy the same output contract and text budget - HF/native image parity: 52.416960 dB PSNR, 0.999723 SSIM ### Cross-BS root cause and fix For the same prompt, seed, and logical request ordinal, the baseline BS4/BS8 trace showed: - initial latent: exact - image embeddings: exact - parent prefix KV: first divergence at transformer layer 1 - step-0 conditional hidden state and velocity: different - step-0 updated latent: different - step-1 latent and velocity: different - final image and re-encoded feature: different - continued greedy text token IDs: exact `cfg_scale=img_cfg_scale=1`, so no unconditioned branch is evaluated and CFG velocity equals conditional velocity. After canonical isolated conditioning, BS4 and BS8 are exact at every traced checkpoint, including the final image, re-encoded feature, and continued decode. ## End-to-End Interleave Performance Headline metric is total client-observed end-to-end wall time. HF concurrency uses simultaneous bounded clients queued behind one official `interleave_gen` model lock because the reference implementation mutates shared KV/current-index state. Native requests are issued simultaneously and use SGLang continuous batching with scheduler-owned parent/child lifecycle management. HF reference timing uses the official in-process `interleave_gen` call. Each HF request enters the bounded model lock, runs a CUDA-synchronized model call, then materializes the shared output contract by base64-encoding the image and JSON-encoding and decoding the response payload. This captures lock queueing, model execution, and equivalent client-side contract serialization, but it does not include a FastAPI server, socket transport, or HTTP framing. Native request wall is measured through the real `/generate` HTTP endpoint and includes request JSON serialization, FastAPI/tokenizer-manager dispatch, scheduler execution, response base64/JSON serialization, socket transfer, JSON parsing, and output-contract materialization. Model/server execution and HTTP/client overhead are reported separately. The headline wall comparison is therefore an official-HF in-process reference versus the native deployed HTTP path, not a claim that the two transport stacks are identical. All values below are measured. No missing batch size is estimated or extrapolated. | Concurrency | HF request median / P95 (s) | Native request median / P95 (s) | HF batch median / P95 (s) | Native batch median / P95 (s) | HF req/s | Native req/s | HF tokens/s | Native tokens/s | Batch wall speedup | Throughput speedup | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 3.7785 / 3.8244 | 3.8811 / 3.9355 | 3.7796 / 3.8253 | 3.8821 / 3.9363 | 0.2641 | 0.2570 | 16.902 | 16.445 | 0.974x | 0.973x | | 2 | 5.7981 / 7.8267 | 4.2385 / 4.2690 | 7.6057 / 7.9047 | 4.2414 / 4.2667 | 0.2612 | 0.4714 | 16.717 | 30.167 | 1.793x | 1.805x | | 4 | 9.6068 / 15.3799 | 4.7805 / 4.8394 | 15.2746 / 15.7867 | 4.7869 / 4.8350 | 0.2606 | 0.8345 | 16.680 | 53.411 | 3.191x | 3.202x | | 8 | 17.4986 / 30.9200 | 6.0621 / 6.0948 | 30.9000 / 31.4323 | 6.0746 / 6.1032 | 0.2576 | 1.3158 | 16.487 | 84.211 | 5.087x | 5.108x | Peak GPU memory: - official HF: 34,842 to 35,792 MiB - native SGLang: 45,534 MiB Model execution and HTTP/client serialization timings are reported separately in the raw and summarized benchmark artifacts. ## T2I/IT2I CUDA Graph Spot Gate The existing public image parity and performance gate remains passed after the interleave fix. | Path | Native median model time (s) | Official HF median (s) | Speedup | HTTP wall median (s) | PSNR | SSIM | Max uint8 diff | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | T2I | 0.070879 | 0.161285 | 2.276x | 0.101458 | 51.4839 dB | 0.999658 | 6 | | IT2I | 0.046370 | 0.167753 | 3.618x | 0.092515 | 52.2700 dB | 0.999657 | 4 | Additional checks: - five measured repeats per path plus one warmup - T2I deterministic PNG SHA-256: `a36c7bd6501ab8e74068086c0f37a817d4fb3475ebed099cd88416ffdacd624d` - IT2I deterministic PNG SHA-256: `5f45aa47e8e255fc13d83110413c521ad2a5023d79d46087bb24e4a86572bd60` - IT2I cached prefix tokens: 550 - server log records `cuda graph: True` for measured 64-token flow batches - real multipart IT2I sends `Content-Length: 40435` and returns HTTP 200 - a chunked multipart request without `Content-Length` fails closed with 411 - live invalid-value probes return HTTP 400 for `n=0`, `num_inference_steps=0`, and `flow_shift=0.0` - an omitted generation `response_format` follows the protocol default `"url"` and returns a `data:image/png;base64,...` URI - GPU cleanup after validation: 1 MiB, 0% utilization, no live compute process ## Warmed Performance Acceptance Final H100 run: one warmup plus five measured repeats per gate, 4096 context, 8192 max total tokens, 16 max running requests, auto truncation disabled. | Gate | Required | Native result | Correctness | Result | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Text BS1 | >=58.4513 tok/s, >=2.5049x | 58.4915 tok/s, 2.5066x | 32/32 exact | PASS | | Text BS8 | >=387.1545 tok/s, >=16.6321x | 387.3900 tok/s, 16.6422x | 8x32 exact | PASS | | Text BS16 | >=729.8184 tok/s, >=31.2222x | 734.9902 tok/s, 31.4435x | 16x32 exact | PASS | | T2I 256x256, 2 steps | <=0.050109s, >=3.2001x | 0.049367s, 3.2482x | deterministic; 48.0578 dB / 0.999247 | PASS | | Fixed-work first image | <=2.350700s, >=2.6785x | 2.296077s server, 2.298605s client, 2.7423x | boundary 125, post 1, deterministic | PASS | Additional acceptance: - exact BS1 graph capture followed by ordinary BS1/8/16 decode remains token exact, proving shared Radix and decode graph coexistence; - malformed exact-text budget and unknown-key requests return HTTP 400; - health remains HTTP 200 after the invalid probes; - final consolidated focused suite: 91 passed, 1 skipped; - final GPU cleanup: 1 MiB, 0% utilization, no live compute process. ## Limitations and Fail-Closed Modes Native interleave deliberately rejects or fails closed for: - overlap scheduling, until per-request lookahead rollback is supported; - speculative decoding; - disaggregated serving; - pipeline parallel size greater than 1; - HiSparse; - Mamba cache layouts; - sessions; - input embeddings or positional-embedding overrides; - logprob, sampling-mask, hidden-state, routed-expert, or indexer-top-k returns; - constrained JSON/regex/EBNF/structural-tag decoding; - context-window overflow after reserving generated image spans; - invalid or excessive image dimensions, pixel counts, flow-step counts, and image-turn counts. Existing request limits remain unchanged: - context length: 4096 - auto truncation: disabled - maximum interleave image turns: 8 - maximum flow steps: 64 - image size and pixel limits remain enforced - image API supports one output image and guidance scale 1 - image-edit masks remain unsupported and are rejected - each parsed edit image is bounded by `media_url_max_file_size_mb` - total edit multipart bytes are capped before parsing at twice the per-file cap plus a fixed 64 KiB multipart/form allowance - absent, duplicate, invalid, understated, or overstated `Content-Length`, interrupted streams, and compressed edit bodies fail closed Internal flow children remain independently batch-isolated and are not inserted into the shared Radix cache. Image response behavior: - generation requests that omit `response_format` inherit the generic protocol default `"url"`; because this integration has no hosted object store, the returned URL is a `data:image/png;base64,...` URI - generation requests with `response_format="b64_json"` return `b64_json` - edit multipart requests default to `response_format="b64_json"` - explicitly passing `response_format=None` to the internal adapter also uses `b64_json` ## Test Commands and Results ### Consolidated unit and graph regression ```bash PYTHONPATH=/mnt/afs/fanyijiat/sensenova_u1_sglang/python \ .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ test/registered/unit/models/test_neo_chat.py \ test/registered/unit/models/test_neo_chat_multimodal.py \ test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_sensenova_u1_images.py \ test/registered/unit/managers/test_sensenova_u1_interleave.py \ test/registered/unit/bench/test_sensenova_u1_interleave_benchmark.py \ test/registered/unit/sampling/test_sampling_batch_info.py \ test/registered/unit/configs/test_model_config.py \ test/registered/unit/model_executor/model_runner_components/test_cuda_graph_setup.py \ test/registered/unit/model_executor/runner/test_prefill_cuda_graph_padding.py \ test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py \ test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_prefill_cuda_graph_runner_helpers.py ``` Result: `142 passed, 1 skipped, 6 subtests passed`. Focused image/API module result: `43 passed`. Warmed-performance continuation result: `91 passed, 1 skipped`. ### Static checks ```bash uv tool run ruff check \ python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_sensenova_u1_images.py \ test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_sensenova_u1_images.py \ test/registered/unit/managers/test_sensenova_u1_interleave.py uv tool run ruff format --check \ python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_sensenova_u1_images.py \ test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_sensenova_u1_images.py git diff --check HEAD^ HEAD ``` Results: - Ruff: PASS - Ruff items.title: config: publish before a process reads configuration
items.body:
Five processes read config namespaces before they published. The launch path
ran validation, port allocation and the subprocess launches ahead of its
publish; the scheduler ran its process configuration first; the tokenizer
manager read the parallel bag in a constructor that is the first publish in a
tokenizer-worker process; the encode server's launch path read the DP size
before the encoder it builds publishes; the detokenizer never published at all
while reading resolution-written fields off the instance it was handed.

Each publishes as early as its config is final -- for the launch path that is
right after late resolution, which refuses a published instance.

The two DSA seed predicates take no config argument: every caller was handing
over the process config, and the fields they read are bag leaves.

items.title: [Fix] Correct dense FP8 Marlin bias ordering
items.body:
## Motivation

Dense FP8 Marlin preparation permuted the bias into the Marlin tile layout. However, the dense wrapper does not pass bias into the Marlin GEMM; it adds bias after the kernel returns. The post-GEMM addition therefore requires the original logical output-channel order. The old behavior produces incorrect biased projections, including the Qwen2 QKV projection.

## Modifications

- Keep dense FP8 Marlin bias in logical output-channel order.
- Continue wrapping the loaded bias as a non-trainable parameter.
- Add a CPU-only regression test in the source-mirrored marlin_utils_fp8 test module.

This applies to all biased dense FP8 Marlin layers. Fused MoE bias handling is unchanged because it follows a separate kernel path.

## Accuracy Tests

Added a CPU-only regression test that uses a non-uniform bias and verifies that Marlin preparation preserves its channel order.

Local validation:

- python3 -m py_compile passed for the changed source and test files.
- git diff --check passed.
- The unit test was not executed locally because the available Python environment does not include PyTorch or pytest; CPU CI will execute it.

Not applicable. The inference-time path is unchanged, and preparation removes an unnecessary bias permutation.

items.title: [Diffusion] Reuse SRT CLIP encoder blocks
items.body:
## Summary

- remove the duplicated CLIP embedding, attention, MLP, and encoder blocks from `multimodal_gen`
- reuse the native SRT CLIP modules and tensor-parallel linear layers while keeping the diffusion output/loader wrappers
- give the shared CLIP attention explicit text-causal vs. vision-bidirectional semantics
- centralize encoder TP-group execution for all native text/image encoders and reused SRT modules
- add a two-GPU tiny-SD3 end-to-end guard for encoder `fold` vs. `replicate`

## Why

The two CLIP implementations had drifted in both behavior and maintenance:

- padded CLIP text input dropped causal masking in the diffusion copy
- SRT CLIP vision attention was accidentally causal
- model blocks, TP loading, and mask handling were implemented twice

Encoder folding also built and sharded a reused SRT encoder under the folding
group, then restored the DiT TP group before forward. SRT layers that resolve
their collective group at execution time could therefore run their folded
weights with the wrong group. Model-specific group patches had started to grow
around this behavior and did not protect every encoder entry point.

`use_tensor_parallel_group` now switches MMGen TP, SRT TP, and SRT attention TP
as one nested context and restores each previous value on exit. Native encoder
roots bind the group used to build their shards through
`EncoderTensorParallelMixin`, so construction, weight loading, and every public
forward use the same group.

The retained CLIP wrappers own only diffusion-specific output selection,
pooling, and weight loading. The duplicated MMGen implementation is removed.

## Validation

- H100, real `openai/clip-vit-base-patch32` BF16 weights: all 148 text and 151 vision parameters loaded
- TP=1 parity after the fix: text (masked and unmasked) and post-norm vision outputs match Transformers exactly
- TP=2: both ranks produce identical outputs; mean absolute difference vs. the replicated BF16 Transformers reference is `0.0141`
- layerwise offload: text and vision encoder stacks are detected and two consecutive streamed runs match resident outputs exactly
- H100 batch=4, 500 measured iterations: vision encoder median `1.814 ms -> 1.584 ms` (`-12.7%`)
- tiny SD3 native e2e, identical 2-GPU Ulysses topology: encoder `fold` vs. `replicate` gives SSIM `0.994886`, PSNR `43.625576`, MAD `0.771159`
- negative control on the pre-fix runtime gives SSIM `0.924886`, PSNR `30.782886`, MAD `5.275228`, and the new e2e fails as intended
- exact final SHA `33a240aa067b5`: standalone fold suite `2 passed`; focused group/folding/SigLIP unit suite `40 passed`
- full pre-commit range passed; no consistency GT or threshold was changed

## Correctness regressions fixed

With the previous CLIP implementation and the same real weights:

- padded text vs. Transformers: max absolute difference `31.375`
- post-norm vision vs. Transformers: max absolute difference `10.5`

Both are `0.0` after this change.

items.title: [diffusion] fix: make MiniMax-H3 AdaLN cache rebuild transactional
items.body:
## Motivation

MiniMax-H3 can rebuild AdaLN outputs from checkpoint weights on demand and memoize the resulting timestep plans across requests. Two cache bookkeeping paths could leave the cache inconsistent:

1. When a new request exceeded `max_plans`, the cache cleared all resident plans but rebuilt only the plans that had been missing before the clear. If the request also reused an existing plan, that plan disappeared from the slab and its later lookup failed during denoising.
2. A plan was added to the host-side `_slots` index before all checkpoint reads and projections completed. If rebuilding raised midway, a retry treated the incomplete plan as a cache hit, skipped rebuilding it, and then failed because its zero `plan_lengths` entry remained invisible to lookup.

The cache also accepted non-positive plan capacities, which could create degenerate slabs and fail later with less actionable errors.

## Modifications

- Rebuild every plan required by the current request after a capacity reset, including plans that were cache hits before the reset.
- Validate the request's plan count and width before clearing resident cache metadata, so an invalid request does not destroy a usable cache.
- Keep new slot assignments in a pending host-side map while checkpoint weights are read and projected.
- Publish `_slots` only after every layer has been written and the corresponding `plan_lengths` entries have been activated. A failed rebuild therefore leaves the incomplete slots invisible and allows a later request to retry.
- Reject non-positive `max_plans` and `max_plan_width` values at cache construction time.

## Accuracy Tests

The change only updates cache admission and metadata publication. It does not change timestep embeddings, checkpoint reads, tensor-parallel sharding, GEMM shapes, collectives, or cached output tensors.

- Forced the capacity-reset path with a request containing both a previously resident plan and a new plan. All plans required by the request remained available to lookup after rebuilding.
- Checked 470,367,744 AdaLN output elements against resident `adaln_proj` projections at both TP1 and TP2: zero mismatches.
- Compared online-rebuild and resident-weight end-to-end outputs at TP1 and TP2. For both cold and cached cases, the online-rebuild MP4 MD5 matched the corresponding resident-weight run.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. This is a correctness-only cache bookkeeping change. The normal successful rebuild path performs the same checkpoint reads, projections, and collectives as before.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
